title: The Try Operator
goal: Unwrap success or early return error using the try operator.

source.attribution: adapted from Day 4 Morning: Error Handling

sections.text: In languages like Python or Java, exceptions bubble up automatically. In Rust, error propagation is explicit using `?`.

sections.caption: The try operator unwraps Ok or returns Err immediately.

sections.text: When attached to a `Result`, `?` evaluates to the inner `Ok` value if successful. If it is an `Err`, the function returns early with that error.
You can only use `?` inside a function that returns a compatible `Result` or `Option` type.

sections.caption: Main can return Result to use the try operator at top level.

sections.text: Converting between different error types with `?` involves trait conversions, which comes next.

explanation: Unwrap success or early return error using the try operator.
